segments.contextAfter: If you’re developing a new app and migrating legacy OpenGL code to Metal, interoperable textures make it easy for you to see the results live as you go.

segments.source: If you’re developing a new app and migrating legacy OpenGL code to Metal, interoperable textures make it easy for you to see the results live as you go.
segments.normalizedSource: If you’re developing a new app and migrating legacy OpenGL code to Metal, interoperable textures make it easy for you to see the results live as you go.
segments.contextBefore: Overview
segments.contextAfter: You can render Metal or OpenGL content into either view by initializing a [`CVPixelBuffer`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/CoreVideo/cvpixelbuffer-q2e) that operates as an interoperable texture.

segments.source: You can render Metal or OpenGL content into either view by initializing a [`CVPixelBuffer`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/CoreVideo/cvpixelbuffer-q2e) that operates as an interoperable texture.
segments.normalizedSource: You can render Metal or OpenGL content into either view by initializing a [`CVPixelBuffer`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/CoreVideo/cvpixelbuffer-q2e) that operates as an interoperable texture.
segments.contextBefore: If you’re developing a new app and migrating legacy OpenGL code to Metal, interoperable textures make it easy for you to see the results live as you go.
segments.contextAfter: When you enable the pixel buffer’s Metal and OpenGL compatibility flags, the textures are capable of being drawn to—and presented by—either rendering technology.
